structural_findings: The architecture's headline contribution — the conflict-free interleaved-BRAM mapping and crossbar permutation — is replaced by a guessed XOR-fold in both impls; the SPECIFIC mapping the paper describes is not reproduced
Twiddle addressing uses generic bit-reversed ROM layout rather than the paper's rearranged twiddle-reuse loop, so the memory-footprint/reuse optimization is structurally absent
Functional Python models do not realize the 9-cycle pipeline (mult 3 + add/sub 1 + Barrett 4 + reg 1) as actual pipeline stages — latency is only asserted as a bound
Radix-4 fusion is modeled as a composition of two radix-2 stages with a j=psi^512 rotator, faithful to the math but not necessarily the paper's symmetric-operator hardware sharing

summary: Reproducibility is solid on the functional layer — all numeric parameters (q, N, psi, omega, Ninv, Barrett constants, widths, 8 BUs) are pinned and both impls agree, with round-trip and negacyclic identities verified — but the spec leaves the paper's actual conflict-free (bank,offset) mapping, crossbar permutation, and twiddle-reuse loop source-missing, forcing both impls to invent the SAME XOR-fold stand-in. That same gap is the biggest fidelity hole: the CFNTT paper's defining contribution (the specific conflict-free memory scheme and bit-reversal-free natural-order datapath) is not actually reproduced — the impls deliver a correct generic negacyclic NTT with the right parameters but not the specific architecture the reference describes.

Twiddle ROM addressing -> standard CT/DIT bit-reversed layout T[k]=psi^bitrev10(k); paper's rearranged-loop addressing f(stage,block) is source-missing
